title: pagefun
summary: Apply matrix operators page-by-page across higher-dimensional arrays.

gpu_support.notes: WGPU provider accelerates batched @mtimes; if no provider hook is present the runtime evaluates on the host and re-uploads numeric results.

description: `pagefun(func, A, B, ...)` applies supported operators independently across pages indexed by third-and-higher dimensions, following MATLAB-compatible pagewise execution semantics.
behaviors: MATLAB-compatible calls require a function handle. In `runmat` compatibility mode, builtin names supplied as character vectors or string scalars are accepted as a RunMat extension.

The first two dimensions of each input form the matrix operated on by the builtin. Dimensions three and up identify individual pages. Inputs with fewer pages are broadcast so long as the page extent is `1`.
Any combination of empty matrices and empty page extents produces empty results with MATLAB-compatible shapes.
MATLAB-compatible calls require at least one distributed or `gpuArray` input. In `runmat` compatibility mode, all-host operands are accepted as a RunMat extension and return host results.

When any operand is a `gpuArray`, provider fallback gathers inputs to the host and uploads uniform real or complex numeric results back to the GPU so documented mixed host/GPU calls preserve output residency.

examples.description: Broadcasting a single page against multiple pages

faqs.question: Which functions does `pagefun` support today?
faqs.answer: RunMat currently supports `@mtimes` page-wise. Additional MATLAB page-aware functions will be added over time as the GPU provider hooks land.

faqs.question: How are page dimensions inferred?
faqs.answer: The first two dimensions represent the matrix operated on by the builtin. Any remaining dimensions are treated as page indices. Inputs with fewer trailing dimensions receive implicit singleton expansion to match other operands.

faqs.question: What happens if the pages are incompatible?
faqs.answer: `pagefun` raises a MATLAB-compatible error describing the mismatched page dimension. Matrix dimension mismatches are forwarded from the underlying builtin (for example, `Inner matrix dimensions must agree` for `@mtimes`).

faqs.question: Are results always uploaded back to the GPU?
faqs.answer: Numeric results are uploaded when every operand started as a `gpuArray` and an acceleration provider is registered. Complex results remain on the host today, matching MATLAB's behaviour when complex GPU buffers are not available.

faqs.question: Does `pagefun` participate in fusion?
faqs.answer: No. Because `pagefun` can invoke arbitrary MATLAB builtins it forms a fusion barrier. Upstream expressions are evaluated before entering `pagefun`.

gpu_residency: No. RunMat's auto-offload planner migrates tensors to the GPU when beneficial. When you explicitly pass any `gpuArray` input, `pagefun` returns supported real or complex numeric results on the device whenever the provider can accept the upload.
gpu_behavior: RunMat Accelerate exposes a custom `pagefun` provider hook. When every operand is a `gpuArray` and the active provider implements the operation (the WGPU backend does for `@mtimes`), pages stay on the device and execute via a tiled compute shader. Mixed host/GPU inputs and unsupported provider operations gather to the host, evaluate using the CPU builtin, and re-upload real or complex numeric outputs so the documented GPU result remains resident.
